meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: But there are very wealthy guests.
They can rent the entire hotel.

examples.text: А вот это тот самый состоятельный гость.
examples.trans: And this is that very wealthy guest.

meanings.en: to see someone out, to see off
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'водить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will escort / walk', paired with 'провожать'.

examples.trans: Please see him out.
I'll see you off.

examples.text: Держи свои духи. Давай я тебя провожу. Пока!
examples.trans: Here is your perfume. Let me walk you out. Bye!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Today is your day off.
Wait, are you Russian?
Stop, bring me a drink, huh?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The hotel is geared toward well-off people.

examples.text: Только обеспеченный человек снимет у нас номер.
examples.trans: Only a wealthy person will book a room with us.
A truly prosperous guest will treat himself to a suite.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'number' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Только обеспеченный человек снимет у нас номер.
examples.trans: Only a wealthy person will book a room with us.

examples.text: Через час у шейха ужин, а это заказ в номер.
examples.trans: In an hour the sheikh has dinner, and this is room service.

examples.text: Давай я отнесу, это молекулярное блюдо, надо в номере доделать.
examples.trans: Let me take it, this is a molecular dish, it must be finished in the room.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'your, yours (polite or plural)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А ваш шеф-повар раздел меня и домогался.
examples.trans: And your head chef undressed me and harassed me.

examples.text: Ваш муж хочет навестить вас после ужина.
examples.trans: Your husband wants to visit you after dinner.
It is your interpreter's fault.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'husband' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: А то я расскажу мужу, что ты видел меня голой.
examples.trans: Otherwise I will tell my husband that you saw me naked.

examples.text: А муж вообще меня раз в месяц посещает.
examples.trans: And my husband only visits me once a month anyway.
And whom will my husband believe?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'wants', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: And he would like to get to know you more closely.
I want coffee.
If you don't want to, suit yourself.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'вестить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to visit'.

examples.text: Ваш муж хочет навестить вас после ужина.
examples.trans: Your husband wants to visit you after dinner.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и навестить вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and to visit on time.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'after', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Take a look at your own face.
Try to make it fast and strong.

examples.text: Вот уйду от тебя, посмотрим, как ты запоёшь.
examples.trans: When I leave you, we will see what tune you sing.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'dinner, supper (evening meal)' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Через час у шейха ужин, а это заказ в номер.
examples.trans: In an hour the sheikh has dinner, and this is room service.

meanings.en: it is necessary, one needs to
meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Шейх Настю? Я тебя умоляю, кому она нужна?
examples.trans: The sheikh, Nastya? I beg you, who needs her?

examples.text: В смысле, Настя, ты мне нужна!
examples.trans: I mean, Nastya, I need you!
I need to step away for a moment.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'надолго'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to step away for a moment.
He left for a short time.

examples.text: Спасибо, я словно ненадолго вернулся домой!
examples.trans: Thank you, I felt as if I briefly returned home!

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'лучиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to step away briefly'.

related.gloss: to to step away briefly (prefixed perfective)
not to to step away briefly (negated infinitive)

examples.trans: I need to step away for a moment.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и отлучиться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and to step away briefly on time.

meanings.en: to answer, to reply, to pick up the phone

examples.text: Она уже целый час не отвечает.

examples.trans: I call you, and you don't answer!

examples.text: Почему ты не отвечаешь на мои вопросы?

meanings.en: urgently, right away; predicative: it is urgent
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'рочно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I urgently need to see Dad!

meanings.en: to see, to catch sight of
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'видеть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to see', paired with 'видеть'.

examples.trans: I urgently need to see Dad!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'daddy' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Pops, take it easy with your words.

examples.trans: Let us hurry to the kitchen.

examples.text: Извините, я ничего не видел, пойду всё переделаю.

meanings.en: to check, to test, to verify

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'hall, corridor' in everyday Russian.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will wait', paired with 'ждать'.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, near, with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'door' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Мы с тобой похожи, как две капли.
